topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture's focus on cancer evolution and outlines the session's key learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how successive genetic mutations and epigenetic alterations confer competitive fitness advantages to drive clonal selection.

topics.label: Cell of origin and the cancer stem cell model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how normal tissue differentiation hierarchies and specific cells of origin determine tumor-propagating capacity.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and inflammatory promotion of tumor growth
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how extrinsic inflammatory signals, environmental promoters, and supportive stroma permit tumor initiation and maintain established neoplasms.

topics.label: Technological methods for investigating tumor biology
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic surveys sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and computational techniques used to analyze cellular interactions and mutational histories in tumors.

topics.label: Integrated multi-factorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how intrinsic mutations, epigenetic plasticity, cell identity, and microenvironmental conditions jointly drive malignant evolution.

topics.label: Closing remarks and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the presentation and introduces the topic for the subsequent lecture.
